(Conditional) Reference identifier for the PAN that enables the SRC system to communicate with the SRCPI without transmitting the actual PAN. 
It is associated with the SRC profile to which the payment card belongs and is unique within an SRC system.
Conditionality: Required when returned to the SRCPI.

dateOfCardCreated.description: UTC time in Unix epoch format. Date when the card was enrolled into the SRC system.

panExpirationYear.description:
Expiration year expressed as a four-digit calendar year (YYYY) for presentation purposes.
Conditionality: Required when specified for the card (PAN).

dateOfCardLastUsed.description: UTC time in Unix epoch format. Date when the card was last used for an SRC transaction.

panExpirationMonth.description:
Expiration month expressed as a two-digit month (MM) for presentation purposes.
Conditionality: Required when specified for the card (PAN).

digitalCardFeatures.description: Attributes related to the digital card features that should be displayed to the consumer.

windowType.description: (Optional) Preferred window type for the authentication method.

challengeIndicator.description:
(Optional) Challenge indicator value related to 3DS authentication. It is one of the following values:
 * 01 - No preference
 * 02 - No challenge requested
 * 03 - Challenge requested (3DS Requestor Preference)
 * 04 - Challenge requested (Mandate)
 * 05 - No challenge requested (transactional risk analysis is already performed)
 * 06 - No challenge requested (Data share only)
 * 07 - No challenge requested (strong consumer authentication is already performed)
 * 08 - No challenge requested (utilize trust list exemption if no challenge required)
 * 09 - Challenge requested (trust list prompt requested if challenge required)

paymentCardTypeSelected.description:
Identifies the cardholder selection to process the transaction as either debit or credit at checkout. 
Applicable only when the card product supports both credit and debit (Combo) options.
Format: It is one of the following values: CREDIT, DEBIT

CustomInputData.description:
Network Specific Custom Input Data.
Clients should silently disregard any unrecognized fields in the JSON object.

PayloadTypeIndicatorCheckout.description:
Identifies the type of encrypted payload to be returned.
Format: It is one of the following values: 
 * FULL — Includes everything; all PCI & PII data (card/token, billing, shipping, consumer)
 * PAYMENT — Includes everything; all PCI & PII data (card/token, billing, shipping, consumer)
 * NON_PAYMENT - Includes only PII data (shipping, billing, consumer); excludes card/token data
 * SUMMARY — (Default) Includes no PCI & PII data; only SRC Profile and transaction metadata

to ensure the authentication result is only delivered to the correct and trusted origin.

dpaPresentationName.description: Display name of the DPA. Required to facilitate transaction authentication.

identityType.description: (Required) Type of consumer identity transmitted or collected.

identityValue.description:
(Required) Consumer identity value that corresponds to the consumer identity type.
Format: String for a valid email address. For a mobile number, use the E.164 format with a maximum length of 15, including the country code. Remove special characters: All spaces, dashes, and parentheses should be removed, and all characters should be numeric. The mobile number must not include "+".

identityProvider.description: (Optional) Identity provider of the Consumer Identity. The default value is SRC

idToken-1.description:
Federated idToken in JWT Format. The token is a JSON Web Token (JWT) compliant with RFC 7519 and signed
using JSON Web Signature (JWS). The API returns the compact serialized JWT string in this field. The decoded JWT structure is 
documented by FederatedIdTokenDecoded, FederatedIdTokenHeader and FederatedIdTokenClaims.
See: #/components/schemas/FederatedIdTokenDecoded

ServiceId.description: To indicate to the SRC System that the Digital Card is the merchant Digital Card-on-file or partner token.

alg.description:
Algorithm used to digitally sign the payload according to RFC 7518.
'none' is not supported. 'PS256' is preferred to 'RS256'.

kid.description: Key ID for the SRC System public key to be used to verify the signature.

typ.description: Media type of the token. For JWT tokens the value should be JWT+ext.id_token.

datePublished.description: Date the resource was published. UTC time in Unix epoch format.

checkoutEventType.description:
Event type associated with the confirmation. Valid values are:
• 00 Place Order
• 01 Authorise
• 02 Capture
• 03 Refund
• 04 Cancel (Auth Reversal)
• 05 Fraud
• 06 Chargeback
• 07 Cancel before Auth
• 08 Auth for account validation
• 09 - 50 EMVCo future use
• 51 - 99 SRC System specific

confirmationReason.description: Description of the reason for the event associated with the order

confirmationStatus.description:
Status related to the checkoutEventType as provided by the SRC Initiator. Valid values are:
• 01 Success
• 02 Failure
• 03 Other
• 04 Timeout

checkoutEventStatus.description:
Event status associated with the order. Valid values are:
• 01 Created
• 02 Confirmed
• 03 Cancelled
• 04 Fraud Cancelled
• 05 Others
• 06 - 50 EMVCo future use
• 51 - 99 SRC System specific

confirmationTimestamp.description: UTC time in Unix epoch format. Date and time of the event set by the SRC Initiator

paymentNetworkReference.description: Transaction identifier as provided by a Payment Network payment authorisation has been completed

(Conditional) Authorisation code associated with an approved transaction

• checkoutEventType is set to 01 (Authorize) or 03 (Refund); and
• confirmationStatus is set to 01 (Success)

networkTransactionIdentifier.description: Unique authorisation related tracing identifier assigned by a Payment Network and provided in an payment authorisation response

identityProvider.description: Identity provider of the consumer identity.

maskedIdentityValue.description: Masked consumer identity value (for example, masked email address or masked mobile phone number).

Use this value in the e-commerce authorization message to VisaNet.
Format: String; maximum 2 digits. It is one of the following values:
05 - Successful authentication
06 - Authentication attempted
07 - Authentication not performed

the SRC system.

clientAppId.description:
(Conditional) Client Application Id, which identifies the wallet provider application.
Format: UUID, 36
Conditionality: Required for Token for Token use-case or deferred authentication flows.

allowPush.description: Consumer's preference for receiving communications via a notification channel.

allowText.description: Consumer's preference for receiving communications via SMS.

allowEmail.description: Consumer's preference for receiving communications via email.

complianceResources.description:

PaymentAccountReference.title: PAR / Payment Account Reference
PaymentAccountReference.description:
A Payment Account Reference (PAR) is a unique reference value associated with a specific card holder PAN. It identifies the card account, not just a card.
PAR is a non-payment identifier that can be associated to PANs and tokens, as defined by EMVCo.  PAR allows all participants in the payments chain to have a single, non-sensitive value assigned to a consumer. This value can be used in place of sensitive card holder identification fields, and transmitted across the payments ecosystem to facilitate card holder identification.
PAR has a well-defined format (as per the Jan 2016 EMVCo documentation):
- Fixed length of 29 characters
- All Uppercase, Roman, & Alphanumeric values
- 4-character BIN Controller ID assigned by EMVCo followed by a 25-character value

endpoints.description:
This API returns Visa's conversion rates for a given currency pair.
  • A request with rateProductCode = "A" returns indicative daily rates that apply to transactions with card as the payment instrument. This is an indicative rate and may be different from the actual rate for settlement of transaction.
    You can use the transactionType field to specify whether you want to obtain foreign exchange rates for PULL or PUSH funds transactions:
    • PULL – Use when the obtain FX rates for Visa Direct Pull Funds transaction.
    • PUSH – Use when the obtain FX rates for Visa Direct Push Funds transaction.
    If transactionType is not provided, the API will return FX rates for Visa Direct Push Funds transaction.
  • A request with rateProductCode = "B" returns indicative daily rates that apply to transactions with bank-account as the payment instrument. This is an indicative rate and may be different from the actual rate for settlement of transaction.
  • A request with rateProductCode = "BANK" returns real-time rates that apply to transactions with bank-account as the payment instrument. This option is only available to clients integrating with “Visa Direct Account and Wallet Send API” bundle.
  • A request with rateProductCode = "WALLET" returns real-time rates that apply to transactions with wallet as the payment instrument. This option is only available to clients integrating with “Visa Direct Account and Wallet Send API” bundle.
The following 3 use cases are supported on the new BANK and WALLET flows:
  1. Provide a currency pair and set quoteIdRequired=true in the FX Request; the response returns a quote ID that can be used on all payout transactions for the same currency pair, until the quote expires.
  2. Provide a currency pair and an amount value in source currency in the FX Request; the response returns a rate and destination amount. This rate and destination amount is only indicative, and not guaranteed to be the same at the time of the payout transaction.
  3. Provide a currency pair and an amount value in destination currency in the FX Request; the response returns a rate and source amount. This rate and source amount is only indicative, and not guaranteed to be the same at the time of the payout transaction.

Please note that the API specifications have been upgraded from swagger 2.0 to OpenAPI 3.0, and clients who have already been accessing this page for Foreign Exchange Rates V2 API documentation may now see a difference in the documentation rendering. However, the API functionality for “A” & “B” rateProductCodes has not changed.
Provide Visa daily currency conversion rate for a given currency pair based on amount

If QuoteIdRequired field is not available in the request, the API behavior is similar to when QuoteIdRequired value is false.

RateProductCode.description:
indicates which rate source to be used like card based vs account based rates.
- A - Card based rates
- B - Account based rates

markupRate.description: The percentage FX mark up rate (<100) to be applied to the transaction.  (Note: The markup is used to estimate how much to collect from a sender and when submitting the OCT payload transaction, the payload must exclude any markup).  Example- A value of 0.07 will assume a 0.07% markup applies to the FX transaction. The default markup rates can also be optionally configured as part of onboarding process. If the markup value is not supplied in the FX inquiry API, and the Acquiring BIN is provided, the markup configured during onboarding will be picked up and applied to the transaction.  To override any markup defaults set up on the account, always send a markup value of 0.00 to indicate 0% markup.

Examples- 99.85, 99.00, etc indicate 2 digits after the decimal point for a 2-exponent currency, 989.333, 989.340, 989.000, etc indicate 3 digits after the decimal point for a 3-exponent currency, & 95, 100 etc indicate no decimal point or minor units for a 0-exponent currency.

Minor currency units after the decimal point, must be less than or equal to the defined currency exponent. This field cannot be 0 or null.
Examples- 99.85, 99.00, etc indicate 2 digits after the decimal point for a 2-exponent currency, 989.333, 989.340, 989.000, etc indicate 3 digits after the decimal point for a 3-exponent currency, & 95, 100 etc indicate no decimal point or minor units for a 0-exponent currency.

systemsTraceAuditNumber.description: This trace number is used to tie together the FX call and the related financial AFT/OCT transaction. For the FX lookup use a value that will be sent in subsequent AFT/OCT transaction.

retrievalReferenceNumber.description:
A value used to tie together the FX call and the related financial AFT/OCT transaction. For the FX lookup use a value that will be sent in subsequent AFT/OCT transaction.

Recommended Format : ydddhhnnnnnn

The first fours digits must be a valid yddd date in the Julian date format, where the first digit = 0-9 (last digit of current year) and the next three digits = 001-366 (number of the day in the year). hh can be the two digit hour in a 24 hour clock (00-23) during which the transaction is performed.

nnnnnn can be the systemsTraceAuditNumber or any 6 digit number.

Prepare the necessary data for a subsequent Authorization Request.

The /oauth2/token endpoint is used to issue, exchange, and refresh tokens for supported authentication flows. It enables scenarios such as device authentication, authorization code to access token or ID token exchange, ID token to access token exchange, and other supported token conversion and renewal operations. This endpoint serves as the central token-processing interface for clients that need to obtain secure tokens after authentication or exchange an existing credential for another token type.
Register a new device instance with authentication keys. Returns a subject_id (device identifier) along with a linkage_url.
Verify the Assertion Response given by the FIDO2 Authenticator to the Relying Party app after a successful navigator.credentials.get() operation.

SigDeviceDynamicData.description:
The content of this field is a JSON Web Signature (JWS). 
Required for Digital Authentication Framework (DAF). Not needed when the signature is generated by the FIDO device.
1. The header of the JWS has these elements:
  “alg”:“...”—Algorithm used for signature
  “kid”:“1234”—Token requestors’s client device ID
  “typ”:“JOSE”
  “cty”:“application/json”—Content type of the content inside JWS
  “iat”:“147...38”—Issued at the timestamp in UTC when the transaction was created and signed.
2. Construct the body as JSON consisting of these:
  vProvisionedTokenID
  the nonce
  clientDeviceID
3. The Signature. When the signature is provided, use this algorithm: RSA-PSS with SHA-256 as the hash and the MGF. Set “algo” to “PS256”

Challenge.description:
A base64url encoded randomized byte string that is to be signed by the authenticator with
The attestation key (associated to an authenticator), during a registration
The credential key (associated to an end-user), during an authentication
According to the Webauthn Spec, this value must have at least 16 bytes of entropy (2^128 bits)
16 random bytes encoded in base64url makes 22 bytes, but it is still only 2^128 bits of entropy
According to the FIDO2 Server Certification documentation, this value must be at most 64 bytes long
Before this value is passed to the FIDO2 authenticator, it must be base64url decoded. This decoded value is the actual challenge given to the authenticator

AttestationObject.description:
The attestation object
The base64Url encoded value of the attestation object that is being registered.
This is the attestation object that is being registered.
It's a structured value as per the WebAuthn specification
It consists of the following
  fmt: the format type in which the attestation is expressed
  attStmt: the attestation statement
    Its contents are specific to the format being used
    Always includes the attestation signature
authData: the authenticator data
    rpIdHash: the sha-256 hash of the rpId (the origin)
    flags: defining bit flags for user present, user verified, backup eligibility (0 - single, 1 - multi device), backup state (0 - not backed up, 1 -backed up), attested credential data present, and extension data present
    signCount: the signature counter (increases with each signature)
   attestedCredentialData
      aaguid: the AAGUID of the authenticator
      credentialIdLength: byte length of the credential id
      credentialId: the FIDO2 credential id
      credentialPublicKey: the COSE encoded public key
   extensions: map with extension identifiers as keys and authenticator extension outputs as values

- 'select_account': The end-user might select an account if multiple sessions with different accounts are already available (not implemented).

AMR.description:

- `otp`: One Time Password. Without qualifier it means totp.
- `pin`: Personal Identification Number.
- `kba`: Knowledge Based Authentication.
- `swk`: Software Secured Key.
- `hwk`: Hardware Secured Key.
- `sc`: Smart Card.
- `fpt`: Fingerprint.
- `face`: Faceprint.
- `iris`: Irisprint.
- `retina`: Retinaprint.
- `vbm`: Voiceprint.
- `rba`: Risk Based Authentication.
- `user`: User Presence.
- `sms`: Short Message Service.
- `tel`: Telephone.
- `geo`: Geolocation.
- `mca`: Multiple Channel Authentication.
- `mfa`: Multiple Factor Authentication.
- `wia`: Windows Integrated Authentication.
- values from OIDC:
- `pop`: Proof of Possession. Similar to swk and hwk without specifying if it is through software or hardware.
- custom values:
- `fed`: Federated.

  - `otp#time`: Time-based OTP.
  - `otp#hash`: Hash-based OTP.
  - `otp#email`: OTP via email.
  - `otp#sms`: OTP via SMS.
  - `otp#txn`: OTP with a payment transaction amount.
- When `amr` is 'pin':
    - `pin#cvv`: PIN with CVV.
- When `amr` is 'tel':
    - `tel#csr`: Telephone with customer service representative.
    - `tel#cb`: Telephone callback.
- When `amr` is 'rba':
    - `rba#rf`: Risk-Based Authentication with refresh token.
    - `rba#aref`: Risk-Based Authentication with activity reference.
    - `rba#sidt`: Risk-Based Authentication with secured ID token.

    - `fed#tds`: Federated with 3DS protocol.

endpoints.description:
service creates a cardholder-selected personal identification number (PIN) for a card that is currently set to the natural PIN (for example, no customer-selected PIN exists). The customer-selected PIN will replace the natural PIN.

The PIN value passed through this API is the cardholder-selected value. The card record allows maintenance regardless of card status or expiration.

The PIN fail count is a program configuration that establishes the maximum number of bad PIN transaction attempts for a card. Successfully creating a card PIN with this service does not reset the PIN fail count. If the maximum PIN fail count for the card has been met, the PIN fail count must be reset on the card record before a cardholder-selected PIN can be established with this API.

The PIN fail count is a program configuration that establishes the maximum number of bad PIN transaction attempts for a card. If the maximum PIN fail count for the card has been met, the PIN fail count must be reset on the card record before a PIN can be updated with this API.

As part of this API service, bad attempts to update a PIN for a card will also contribute to the PIN fail counter. As long as requests are valid, there is no limit to the number of times a PIN can be updated. The card record allows maintenance regardless of card status or expiration.

If creating a new card ID prior to calling this API, allow time for data synchronization between the Create Card ID response and this API request. When a card is replaced, a new card ID must be requested.

The DPS Debit Card Search API retrieves a list of Primary Account Numbers (PANs) associated with the search criteria provided. Possible search criteria options are account number and routing number, name, customer ID, card replacement number (CRN), and member number. Only one search criteria is supported per request.

The initial card number may have expired but the lifecycle could have been extended, keeping the card in good standing. Cards returned may be active or inactive. Inactive cards are still eligible to be activated to perform transactions.

accountId.description: The account ID uniquely identifies account(s) associated to the card ID.

currencyCode.description: 3-character ISO currency code. Applicable only if balances are returned.

accountNumber.description:
The account number is a funding source for the card. A card can have one or many accounts. For financial institutions, this generally refers to the checking account or savings account number.

Not applicable to Prepaid.

institutionId.description:
Identifies a client at DPS. This field is assigned by DPS and may appear on client reports. A client may be assigned multiple institution IDs as needed.

Not applicable to Prepaid.

ledgerBalance.description: Ledger balance can be equal to, greater than or less than available balance depending on subsequent settlement of pending transactions and deposits.

accountTypeCode.description: Account type code is an abbreviated code used to identify account type in DPS Debit and is a required field at account creation.

availableBalance.description: Available balance in default account currency. Amount available to use in this account.

fundingIndicator.description:
For point of sale (POS) activity, this field defines the funding account that is assigned to a transaction when the service line of the transaction is not known. Typically, primary and funding accounts are the same but can be different for investment accounts or other non-standard card-to-account associations.

Not applicable to Prepaid.

accountOpenedDate.description:
Assigned by client to identify date the account was established. The value is in UTC and the format is yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ss.SSS'Z'.

Not applicable to Prepaid.

creditLineBalance.description:
Credit line balance is applicable to credit account types. Maximum credit applicable for the line of credit.

Not applicable to Prepaid.

isFundingComputed.description:
For POS activity, if the client did not set any accounts as a funding account, DPS Debit system uses other fields (DDA, Primary, other) to identify whether funding indicator is set by the client or is computed by DPS.

Not applicable to Prepaid.

accountIndicatorCode.description: This field is only used for ATM services, where multiple account selections are available.

accountTypeDescription.description:
Account type assigned to the account when it was created from a pre-defined enumeration list. In DPS Debit, this is an optional field at account creation.

Not applicable to Prepaid.

availableCreditBalance.description:
Available credit balance is applicable to credit account types. Difference between credit used and maximum credit balance.

Not applicable to Prepaid.

lastBalanceUpdateTimeStamp.description: Date/time account balance was changed. The value is in UTC and the format is yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ss.SSS'Z'.

accountIndicatorDescription.description:
Account indicator description matches the selected account indicator code.

Not applicable to Prepaid.

prcId.description: The Issuer (PRC) level for U.S. card programs processed by Visa DPS.

netTotal.description: Net Total of items 2 through 9 (should be equal to 1) Net total of line items 2 through 8. This net total should equal line item 1, the daily wire transfer amount.

differences.description: Difference The difference between line items 1 and 9.

wireTotalAmount.description: Wire Total Amount Total dollar amount of the wire transfer. This is a net total of all credit transactions less all debit transactions, applicable fees, and dispute items.

processorSettlementAmount.description: Processor Settlement Report EF500210-RP03 Provides the net total of all cardholder activity and terminal activity processed through Visa DPS. This net total represents activity settled by Visa DPS for the current business date. The net cardholder and terminal activity are reported on the Processor Settlement Report EF500210-RP03.

miscellaneousFeesSettlementAmount.description: Miscellaneous Fees Settlement Detail DD0716-D02 Provides the net total of administrative fees initiated and received by your institution. This net total represents activity settled for the current VisaNet business date. The net issuer and acquirer total is reported on the Miscellaneous Fees Settlement Summary DD0716-D01, D02.

exceptionTransactionSettlementAmount.description: Exception Transaction Settlement Detail DD0714-D02 Provides the net total of all chargebacks, representments, and adjustments. This net total represents activity settled by the networks and passed to Visa DPS for the current business date. The net issuer and acquirer total is reported on the Exception Transactions Settlement Detail and Summary reports DD0714-D01, D02.

01 – Fraud loss due to card stolen

UCAFField.description: This field contains Mastercard e-commerce Universal Cardholder Authentication data in encrypted form. It may also contain Mastercard telephone order data.

UCAFCollectionIndicator.description: E-commerce indicator that Mastercard Universal Cardholder Authentication data is included in the message.

transactionLinkIdentifier.description: Transaction Link Identifier returned from other networks like MasterCard and Pulse

secureRemoteTokenCryptogram.description: This field contains Mastercard digital payment/Cryptogram data associated with the token.

remoteCommerceAcceptorIdentifier.description: This field contains a merchant identifier encoded as Base64. For example website URL or reverse domain name.

payoutId.description: For a Push transaction the identifier of Pull transaction that funds it can be provided, to associate the Pull and Push transactions

surcharge.description:
When present, this field contains surcharge as assessed by the Originating Entity. Values in this field must be included in the transactionAmount and should be in the same currency and format as defined in the transactionAmount field.

Note: if card credential is provided in senderDetail, fund is debited by transactionAmount from sender's card; but credited by transactionAmount - surcharge to recipient's card
Technical Specifications - Appendix E Country and Currency codes for VDC.

sencondaryId.description: secondaryId is used for C2B use case in the CEMEA region where payee initiates the OCT to the payer. The merchant or acquirer may use this field to obtain an Agreement Id in order to process the request.

motoECIIndicator.description:
Identifies the level of security used in an electronic commerce transaction over an open network (for example, the Internet) or the type of mail or telephone order. Acquirers supply indicator values, which Visa forwards in requests and advices to issuers that have successfully tested to receive them. The subfield is dropped if issuers have not successfully completed testing or choose not to receive it.
If not provided, Visa will default its value to 7 for US and 5 for rest of the world, for e-Commerce transaction

purposeOfPayment.description:
Purpose of payment code is required in certain markets to clearly identify the purpose of the payment based on the standard values defined for respective market

Conditional (Refer to Payouts Endpoint Guide on country-specific required fields and lengths)

ISO20022 field name: Purpose of Payment

messageReasonCode.description:
Conditional.

Contains codes that combined with some other fields such as the BAI (Business Application Id) identify some unique use cases. For Sales Tax rebates this field should be populated with the value 5120 (Value-added tax/Sales Tax) along with the businessApplicationId field set to the value 'FD' which indicates this push funds transfer is being conducted in order to facilitate a sales tax refund.

transactionAmount.description:
This field contains the transaction amount in the currency specified by the currency code in 'transactionCurrencyCode'. 
The amount of POS funds requested by the cardholder, expressed in the local currency in an original authorization or financial transaction. 
This field also contains the acquirer-assessed surcharge.            

Note: Transaction amount should be numeric. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide on country-specific currency minor units. Refer to SMS POS Visa & Visa Electron
Technical Specifications - Appendix E Country and Currency codes for Card.

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JOD is 3, the amount is JOD 100.996.

feeProgramIndicator.description: Note: If present, a valid value is required. Spaces or special characters are not allowed.

businessApplicationId.description:
Business Application Identifier (BAI) identifies the type of program for which the payment is being sent, i.e. whether it is a funds disbursement, money transfer etc. It should be a valid value allowed by Visa and approved for the program during onboarding.

Valid BAI for Push to Cards:
- Money transfer: AA, PP, BI, FT, WT; 
- Non-money transfer: BB, BP, CP, FD, GD, GP, LO, MD, OG, PD, PS

transactionCurrencyCode.description:
The 3-character ISO-4217 code in this field reflects the currency associated to the transaction amount 
Format: 3-character ISO-4217 (Alpha-3) currency code

ISO20022 field name: Instructed Amount Currency Code

localTransactionDateTime.description:
The date and time when the transaction takes place, expressed in the local time of the Originating Entity request

Format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss

ISO20022 field name: Message Creation Date Time

name.description: Name of the cardAcceptor

terminalId.description: The identifier for the terminal at a card acceptor location

VerificationCardAcceptor.description: The cardAcceptor is the merchant, funds transfer originator, or Visa internal application submitting the Payment Account Validation request

SchemeIdentifier.description: Scheme identifier for the card, "01" Visa, "02" Other

transactionCurrencyCode.description:
3-digit numeric or 3-character alpha ISO currency code of the transaction as expressed in the amount field. This can be either:
  • The originator's chosen currency for the transaction OR
  • The recipient's card currency (refer to the billingCurrencyCode obtained from the Eligibility Check for Card API)*
Adjust amount accordingly based on chosen transactionCurrencyCode.
*Note: This currency may not always be the local currency code of the recipient.

Refer to ISO Codes

optionalResponseParameters.description: Comma-separated list of optional response parameters to include in the response

OCTTransactionDetail.description: Transaction details for Original Credit Transaction

nameMatch-2.description: Score provided based on recipient’s name match, if recipient’s account is found and active. Supports below values: STRONG_MATCH,PARTIAL_MATCH and NO_MATCH. STRONG_MATCH - Recipient’s account found and name is a highly confident match. PARTIAL_MATCH - Recipient’s account found and name is a partial match. NO_MATCH - Recipient’s account found but name is likely not a match. Applicable only for Accounts.

nameMatch-1.description:
Score provided based on recipient’s name match, if recipient’s account isfound and
active. Supports below values: STRONG_MATCH,PARTIAL_MATCH,NO_MATCH. STRONG_MATCH-
Recipient’s account found and name is a highly confident match. PARTIAL_MATCH-
Recipient’s account found and name is a partial match. NO_MATCH- Recipient’s account
found but name is likely not a match. Applicable only for Accounts.

RecipientDateOfBirth.description: Recipient date of birth (Format: "YYYY-MM-DD", e.g. "1980-02-01"). ISO20022 field name: Creditor Birth Date.

SpecialConditionIndicatorMerchant-1.description:
Cryptocurrency indicator with the value of “7” can be used to identify the purchase of cryptocurrency, thereby providing greater visibility to the issuers.
  - 1 – Purchase of Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) or Tokenized Deposits
  - 2 – Purchase of Stablecoin (fiat-backed)
  - 3 – Purchase of Blockchain Native Token/Coin
  - 4 – Purchase of Non-Fungible Token (NFT)
  - 7* - Purchase of Cryptocurrency

settlementAmount.description: This is the amount to be debited from Originating Entity/Visa Client's funding account.

destinationAmount.description:
The destination amount that will be deposited to the recipient account, expressed in the Recipient bank currency code provided in the original request. If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the recipient bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

Note: Destination amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Visa Direct Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units.

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Instructed Amount

metadataVersion.description:
This is the version of the updated route definition. 
It is in the format <major-version>.<minor-version>.<patch>.

* patch updates are documentation updates only and should not influence the processing of a payout transaction. Example: changes to the description of Purpose of Payment code.

* minor-version updates indicate backward compatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Example: addition of a new Purpose of Payment code.

* major-version updates indicate backward incompatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Such changes are usually regulatory in nature or due to partner migration on Visa's backend. Example: Purpose of Payment code changing from a "conditional"/ "recommended" to a "required" field.

metadataVersion.description:
This is the version of the route definition recalled by VISA. 
It is in the format <major-version>.<minor-version>.<patch>.

* patch updates are documentation updates only and should not influence the processing of a payout transaction. Example: changes to the description of Purpose of Payment code.

* minor-version updates indicate backward compatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Example: addition of a new Purpose of Payment code.

* major-version updates indicate backward incompatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Such changes are usually regulatory in nature or due to partner migration on Visa's backend. Example: Purpose of Payment code changing from a "conditional"/ "recommended" to a "required" field.

Secure Corporate Payment (SCP) Indicator.

Valid Values :

This field maps to ISO8583->TLV Field 34, Dataset ID 4A, Tag 88.

scaEnvironmentOutageIndicator.description:
Acceptance Environment Authentication Outage Indicator.

Valid Values :
FALSE - No authentication outage
TRUE - Authentication outage

If this exemption does not apply to the transaction, the value of "FALSE" is optional and the field may be omitted entirely.This field maps to ISO8583 Field 34 – Dataset ID 02 -Tag 87.

delegatedAuthenticationIndicator.description:
Delegated Authentication Indicator.

Valid Values :
FALSE - Delegated authentication not claimed/requested
TRUE - Delegated authentication claimed/requested

If this exemption does not apply to the transaction, the value of "FALSE" is optional and the field may be omitted entirely.
Clients requesting this exemption should also provide the the following request parameters:
1. visaMerchantIdentifier value, which is an unique identifier assigned by Visa for each merchant included in the identification program.Issuers can obtain a list of Visa-assigned merchant identifiers from Visa Online (VOL).
2. Cardholder Authentication Verification Value (CAVV) OR Token Authentication Verification Value (TAVV)

Program Qualification: Acquirers that choose to participate will identify and qualify potential Delegates that meet the qualification criteria and work with them to evidence how their authentication capabilities are compliant and to obtain their agreement to the requirements of the Program through the Readiness Questionnaire. CurrencyInfoReason.description:
The reason denotes why a particular currency change has happened.
1. FLEXIBLE_SETTLEMENT_DISABLED – The flexible settlement is disabled for the client. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED. 
2. CURRENCY_DISABLED - The currency is disabled for the client. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
3. FREEZE_MANUAL – The currency has been manually frozen. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
4. FREEZE_SETTLEMENT_DUE - The currency is automatically frozen following a settlement breach and will stay frozen until the outstanding amount is paid. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
5. FREEZE_ALL_FREEZE_ENABLED - This currency is frozen because another currency is overdue, and the all-freeze setting is enabled. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
6. UNFREEZE_MANUAL - The currency has been manually enabled temporarily. This applies only when the currentStatus is ENABLED.
7. NO_DUES - The currency is enabled and can be used to send payouts. This applies only when the currentStatus is ENABLED.

groupName.description:
The name of the metadata element/enum.
This generic Identity Group object can represent either 'Recipient Identity Field Group object' or 'Bank Account Registration Field Group object' . 
Enum value signifies the particular metadata element. 

For example : 
 a) if enum is "address", this can contain array of 'IdentityField' object where each object can represent elements like addressLine1, addressLine2, city, countryCode, postalCode etc    

 b) enum can be "identificationList", which contains array of "IdentityField' objects, one of the IdentityField object can have elementName="idType" and inputType="list", in this scenario array of IdentityListItem will have 
 [
   {
     "label": "Passport",
     "value": "Passport"
   },
   {
     "label": "National ID Card",
     "value": "National ID Card"
   },
   {
     "label": "Driving License",
     "value": "Driving License"
   }
 ], 
 second 'IdentityField' Object -> elementName as "identificationNumber" with inputType="text" 
 third 'IdentityField' Object -> elementName as "identificationCountry" with inputType="text" 
 fourth 'IdentityField' Object -> elementName as "validFromDate" with inputType="text"
 fifth  'IdentityField' Object -> elementName as "validToDate" with inputType="text" and so on.

 c) If enum is "additionalData",this will have array of two 'IdentityField' objects, one representing 'additionalDataKey' and other one 'additionalDataValue'.

 d) If enum is "name", "middleName" may be required for some countries (e.g. Africa). This can be accommodated by appending a space and then middleName to <firstName>

payoutMethod.description: Payout method code. Valid values are B- Bank , W- Wallet (This ENUM is not currently supported. It is for future use.)

notificationId.description: Unique identifier for the notification. In case of a recall (i.e., when the notificationType is "RECALL"), this field will contain the notificationId of a previously sent notification that is being recalled.

metadataVersion.description:
This is the version of the route definition recalled by VISA. 
It is in the format <major-version>.<minor-version>.<patch>.

* patch updates are documentation updates only and should not influence the processing of a payout transaction. Example: changes to the description of Purpose of Payment code.

* minor-version updates indicate backward compatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Example: addition of a new Purpose of Payment code.

* major-version updates indicate backward incompatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Such changes are usually regulatory in nature or due to partner migration on Visa's backend. Example: Purpose of Payment code changing from a "conditional"/ "recommended" to a "required" field.

metadataVersionDate.description: This was the expected go-live date of the recalled metadata version.

fxConversionRate.description: This field contains the exchange rate applied to the pair of settlementCurrencyCode and destinationCurrencyCode

settlementAmount.description: This is the amount to be debited from Originating Entity/Visa Client's funding account.

destinationAmount.description:
The destination amount that will be deposited to the beneficiary account, expressed in the destination currency code provided in the original request. If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the beneficiary bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

identificationNumberBusiness

Conditional.

This is an alphanumeric value that carries the recipient's identification number issued to the recipient by the government or an authorized national entity. This field is to be used if the recipient is a business (e.g. Disbursements)

If recipientIdentificationNumberIndividual is not populated, then this field needs to be populated mandatorily for Brazil domestic trasactions when businessApplicationId has any of the below values:

AA
PP
TU
BI
WT
FT

For Argentina domestic purchase transactions this field contains the merchant’s value-added tax (VAT) registration number or single business reference number (SBRN).

identificationNumberIndividual

Conditional.

This field contains the identification number issued to the individual by the government or an authorized national entity. For Argentina domestic purchase transactions this field contains the customer’s VAT registration number for tax identification.

If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the beneficiary bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

masterCardPartnerIdCode

Conditional.

This field identifies a specific partnership agreement, generally between specific acceptors and issuers. may be used for transactions on accounts issued under co-branding agreements when one of the co-branding partners originates the transaction.

This field is conditionally required for all MasterCard transactions.

masterCardIndependentSalesOrganizationId

Conditional.

This field contains the "Company ID" that is assigned during the time of registration with Mastercard Connect as a service provider and must be provided by the acquirer.

This field is conditionally required for all MasterCard transactions.

masterCardSubMerchantId

Sub-Merchant ID containing the sponsored merchant ID. This field is conditionally required when a payment facilitator is involved and for all MasterCard transactions.

masterCardMerchantPaymentGatewayId

This field contains merchant payment gateway ID assigned by Mastercard, provided by the acquirer when a registered merchant payment gateway service provider participates in the transaction. Value is right-justified and zero-filled.

merchantPseudoAbaNumber

This is a number that uniquely identifies the originator when they sign up to send Push Payment Gateway transactions. On enrollment, an originator will get a single pseudo-value that is assigned by Visa. The other networks will assign their own unique values for the originator.

Note:
Supported only in US for domestic transactions involving Push Payments Gateway Service.

The destination amount that will be deposited to the recipient account, expressed in the destination currency code provided in the original request. CurrencyInfoReason-1.description:
The reason denotes why a particular currency change has happened.
1. FLEXIBLE_SETTLEMENT_DISABLED – The flexible settlement is disabled for the client. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED. 
2. CURRENCY_DISABLED - The currency is disabled for the client. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
3. FREEZE_MANUAL – The currency has been manually frozen. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
4. FREEZE_SETTLEMENT_DUE - The currency is automatically frozen following a settlement breach and will stay frozen until the outstanding amount is paid. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
5. FREEZE_ALL_FREEZE_ENABLED - This currency is frozen because another currency is overdue, and the all-freeze setting is enabled. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
6. UNFREEZE_MANUAL - The currency has been manually enabled temporarily. This applies only when the currentStatus is ENABLED.
7. NO_DUES - The currency is enabled and can be used to send payouts. This applies only when the currentStatus is ENABLED.

name.description:
masterCardPartnerIdCode

Conditional.

This field identifies a specific partnership agreement, generally between specific acceptors and issuers. may be used for transactions on accounts issued under co-branding agreements when one of the co-branding partners originates the transaction.

This field is conditionally required for all MasterCard transactions.

masterCardIndependentSalesOrganizationId

Conditional.

This field contains the "Company ID" that is assigned during the time of registration with Mastercard Connect as a service provider and must be provided by the acquirer.

This field is conditionally required for all MasterCard transactions.

masterCardSubMerchantId

Sub-Merchant ID containing the sponsored merchant ID. This field is conditionally required when a payment facilitator is involved and for all MasterCard transactions.

masterCardMerchantPaymentGatewayId

This field contains merchant payment gateway ID assigned by Mastercard, provided by the acquirer when a registered merchant payment gateway service provider participates in the transaction. Value is right-justified and zero-filled.

merchantPseudoAbaNumber

This is a number that uniquely identifies the originator when they sign up to send Push Payment Gateway transactions. On enrollment, an originator will get a single pseudo-value that is assigned by Visa. The other networks will assign their own unique values for the originator.

Note:
Supported only in US for domestic transactions involving Push Payments Gateway Service.

fxConversionRate.description: This field contains the exchange rate applied to the pair of settlementCurrencyCode and destinationCurrencyCode

settlementAmount.description: This is the amount to be debited from Originating Entity/Visa Client's funding account.

destinationAmount.description:
The destination amount that will be deposited to the recipient account, expressed in the Recipient bank currency code provided in the original request. If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the recipient bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

Note: Destination amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Visa Direct Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units.

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Instructed Amount

transactionAmount.description:
The amount to debit from merchant's funding account or credit to recipient's bank account.

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Visa Direct Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Instructed Amount

returnCurrencyCode.description:
The 3-character ISO-4217 code in this field reflects the currency associated with the returnAmount value. It will be same as the client’s settlement currency against the original payout transaction.

ISO20022 field name: Payment Return - Instructed Amount Currency Code

SourceOfFunds-1.description:
Sender source of funds indicator i.e. the funding method used by the sender to fund the payout.Valid values are:
Conditional - source of funds is required by some endpoints, please check for Visa Payment Guide for details  

01 = Visa credit
02 = Visa debit
03 = Visa prepaid
04 = Cash
05 = Deposit accounts other than those linked to a Visa card (includes checking/savings accounts and proprietary debit/ATMcards)
06 = Credit accounts other than those linked to a Visa card (includes credit cards and proprietary credit lines)

Note: For any Company to Company (C2C) or Company to Individual (C2I) use-case, this should be “05”, since the funds come from the sender’s bank account. This field is required for Money Transfers and Funds Disbursements.

amount.description:
Funding amount that is credited by the Originating Entity. Expressed in the currency provided in field currencyCode

Funding amount should be numeric and  decimal is not allowed. Please refer to Visa Direct Payouts - Endpoint Guide on currency exponent for each market

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2. If the transaction amount is $100.99, then this field should populate “10099”. If the transaction amount is $100.00 then this field should populate “10000”. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the transaction amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

version.description:
This is the version of the metadata response. 
It is in the format \<major-version-number\>.\<minor-version-number\>.\<minor-sub-version-number\>.

* minor-sub-version-number updates are documentation updates only and should not influence the processing of a payout transaction. Example: changes to the description of Purpose of Payment code.

* minor-version-number updates indicate backward compatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Example: addition of a new Purpose of Payment code.

* major-version-number updates indicate backward incompatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Such changes are usually regulatory in nature or due to partner migration on Visa's backend. Example: Purpose of Payment code changing from a "recommended" to a "required" field.

amount.description: This is the amount of money remitted for the referred document. Note that this field accepts signed amounts. A positive amount value indicates amounts flowing in the direction of the payout transaction, and due to the recipient . A negative amount value indicates the amount due back to the sender, i.e. a reduction in the total remitted amount. An amount value without the explicit mention of sign would be assumed positive.

approvalCode.description:
This is a unique authorization code for an approved transaction from Issuer

cardAcceptorId.description: An identifier that uniquely identifies the Originating Entity.  For Push to Card transactions, Card Acceptor Terminal ID (CAID) should be populated

transactionAmount.description:
This field contains the transaction amount in the currency specified by the currency code in 'transactionCurrencyCode'. 
The amount of POS funds requested by the cardholder, expressed in the local currency in an original authorization or financial transaction. 
This field also contains the acquirer-assessed surcharge.            

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Instructed Amount

originalActionCode.description: Contains a code that provides the result of original payout request when current request is identified as duplicate of original and actionCode will be 94.

systemTraceAuditNumber.description: This field contains a number generated by Visa that uniquely identifies a transaction and all message types. The trace number is a key data element used to match a response to its request or to match a message to others for a given transaction set

transactionCurrencyCode.description:
The 3-character ISO-4217 code in this field reflects the currency associated to the transaction amount. 

Format: 3-character ISO-4217 (Alpha-3) currency code

Example: "PHP"

enablerVerificationValue.description: Only applicable for pull reversal for CardsEnabler Verification Value (EVV) is a Visa assigned value that is used to identify enablers that participate in certain programs. The EVV is unique to the enabler.

retrievalReferenceNumber.description:
This is a unique identifier generated by Visa for a card transaction

The format is ydddhhnnnnnn
yddd - The first four digits must be a valid Julian date format, where the first digit = 0-9 (last digit of current year) and the next three digits = 001-366 (number of the day in the year). 
hh - can be the two digit hour in a 24 hour clock (00-23) during which the transaction is performed. 
nnnnnn - can be the systemsTraceAuditNumber or any 6 digit number

PendingCancelledTransactionStatus.description:
- PENDING: Payout is accepted but has not been acknowledged
- PENDING_CANCELLATION: Cancel payout status is pending
- CANCELLED - Payout is cancelled when in pending status

condition.description: It refers to an 'id' value in the conditions[] array.

maxAmountValue.description: The maximum amount value allowed per transaction.

currencyOfMaxAmount.description: The (Alpha-3) ISO-4217 currency code of the maximum amount value allowed per transaction. This could be in recipient bank currency or in a more common currency like USD, EUR or GBP.

status.description:
Status of the transaction, only received in 202
- PAYMENT_RECEIVED: Visa has acknowledged the payout instruction has been received. Only happens in 202.

This is a unique identifier generated by the Visa for the original payout

ISO20022 field name: Transaction Information And Status - Original Additional Remittance Information

fxConversionRate.description: This field contains the exchange rate applied to the pair of settlementCurrencyCode and destinationCurrencyCode

settlementAmount.description: This is the amount to be debited from Originating Entity/Visa Client's funding account.

destinationAmount.description:
The destination amount that will be deposited to the beneficiary account, expressed in the destination currency code provided in the original request. If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the beneficiary bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Transaction Information And Status - Remitted Amount

transactionAmount.description:
The amount to debit from merchant's funding account or credit to beneficiary's bank account.

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Instructed Amount

fundsAvailableDateTime.description: Funds available Date and Time of the payment

settlementCurrencyCode.description:
The settlement currency code

The 3-character ISO-4217 code in this field reflects the currency for the Settlement amount to be debited from Originating Entity/Visa Client's funding account.

Format: 3-character ISO-4217 (Alpha-3) currency code

Example: GBP

The format is ydddhhnnnnnn. yddd - The first four digits must be a valid Julian date format, where the first digit = 0-9  (last digit of current year) and the next three digits = 001-366 (number of the day in the year). hh - can be the two digit hour in a 24 hour clock (00-23) during which the transaction is performed. nnnnnn - can be the systemsTraceAuditNumber or any 6 digit number.

AFTRSenderCard.description: Card details for the sender in an Account Funding Transaction Reversal

motoECIIndicator.description: Identifies the level of security used in an electronic commerce transaction over an open network (for example, the Internet) or the type of mail or telephone order. Acquirers supply indicator values, which V.I.P. forwards in requests and advices to issuers that have successfully tested to receive them.

last4ofPAN.description: This field contains the last four digits of the cardholder primary account number (PAN)

chipCardData.description: A blob containing the Chip card data in TLV format

exchangeRate.description: PFX Exchange Rate decimal

visaRateTableId.description: Rate table Id of the PFX exchange rate

visaRateProvider.description: Provider of the PFX exchange rate

memberComments.description: This field can be optionally used to send and receive comments by service providers. Issuers can optionally include new text in this field in the response. If the issuer does not include this field, Visa will inject the value from the request in the response and send it back to the service provider.

prepaidBalance.description:
Min Inclusive: -999999999.999

dafIndicator.description:
An authentication program indicator to identify transactions qualified by the Digital Authentication Framework for requests containing a CAVV and/or TAVV.
Possible values are true or false

customerReference.description:
Conditional

This field contains a value that identifies the customer.

responseReasonCode.description: This field contains the merchant advice code value received from Mastercard authorization response messages.

exemptionReasonCode.description:
One or more instances of reason codes that explain why an exemption was not honored.

Valid Values :
8A01 = Merchant not participating in Visa Delegated Authentication Program
8A02 = Issuer not participating in Visa Delegated Authentication Program
8A04 = Indeterminate or invalid issuer response
8A06 = Did not meet exemption criteria (Visa determined)
8A07 = VMID invalid for service
8A08 = CAVV invalid value
8A76 = Did not meet delegation criteria (Issuer supplied)
8473 = Cardholder has not trusted the merchant (issuer supplied)
8474 = Did not meet the exemption criteria (issuer supplied)
8976 = Did not meet exemption criteria (issuer supplied)

This field is present in API response only if any of the SCA exemptions were claimed and optionalResponseParameters field was set to include "RISKASSESSMENTDATA" as one of the comma separated values in the API request.

This field maps to ISO8583 Field 34, Dataset ID 4A- Tag 8C.

scpExemptionIndicator.description:

This field maps to ISO8583 Field 34 – Dataset ID 4A -Tag 88.

traExemptionIndicator.description:

lowValueExemptionIndicator.description:
This field is present in API response only if the following conditions are met.

- optionalResponseParameters field was set to include "RISKASSESSMENTDATA" as one of the comma separated values in the API request.

- Low Value exemption was claimed in the acquirer request (OR) Issuer chooses to approve the transaction as the amount was below the issuer set low value and velocity counts limits

delegatedAuthenticationIndicator.description:

trustedMerchantExemptionIndicator.description:

riskAssessmentResults.description: This object is present in the response only if the issuer supports SCA exemptions.

reimbursementAttribute.description:

cardAuthenticationResults.description: A Visa-defined code indicating Online Card Authentication Method results. Refer to cardAuthenticationResults

integratedCircuitCardData.description: A blob containing the Chip card data in TLV format.

mvvAcquirerAssigned.description: Visa assists the acquirer in assigning the last four. E.g. 98FC

merchantVerificationValue.description: Merchant Verification Value(MVV) is used to identify merchants that participate in a variety of programs. The MVV is unique to the merchant.

transactionLinkIdentifier.description: Transaction Link Identifier returned from other networks like MasterCard and Pulse

addressVerificationResults.description:
Results of the Address Verification Service (AVS) validation for the Primary Account Number.
Refer to addressVerificationResults

recipientIdentificationNumberIndividual.description: Unique identifier for the recipient individual. This is used to identify the recipient in the system.

cpsAuthorizationCharacteristicsIndicator.description:

Please reach out to your Visa representative for details.

name.description:
Recipient company name. Full name is conditionally required when "firstName" and "lastName" are not provided.
Must have at least 3 chars
Must not contain exclusively numeric characters
Must not contain special symbols
!"£ $ % ^ * + = ¬ ¦ : ; @ ~

type.description: Identifies the type of recipient - "U" for Unspecified(whether Individual or Company).

cityOfBirth.description:
Recipient city of birth

Recipient country of birth

OriginatorId.description:
An alphanumeric field that uniquely identifies the Originating Entity for Push to Account transactions. The Orignating Entity should populate Card Acceptor ID (CAID)  for Push to Card transactions. 

ISO20022 field name: Debtor - Originating Entity Identification

shareLink.description:
An optional field that includes a URL (shareLinkURL) directing the sender to WeChat, where they can view the transaction status. The link can be shared with the recipient to prompt them to fulfill any requirements for receiving their funds.
Currently, this is applicable only for Visa Direct wallet payments to the WeChat wallet operator.

traceable.description: Indicates if a payout transaction is traceable

recallable.description: Indicates if a payout transaction is recallable

paymentRail.description: Indicates the payment rail used for the payout transaction

isFinalStatus.description: Only populated at PAYMENT_SENT status, indicates whether that is the final status provided by network partner.

status.description:
Status of the transaction, only received in 202
- PAYMENT_RECEIVED: Visa has acknowledged the payout instruction has been received. Only happens in 202.
ISO20022 field name: Transaction Information And Status - Transaction Status

payoutId.description:
This is a unique identifier generated by the Visa for the original payout

ISO20022 field name: Transaction Information And Status - Original Additional Remittance Information

fxConversionRate.description: This field contains the exchange rate applied to the pair of settlementCurrencyCode and destinationCurrencyCode

settlementAmount.description: This is the amount to be debited from Originating Entity/Visa Client's funding account.

destinationAmount.description:
The destination amount that will be deposited to the recipient account, expressed in the destination currency code provided in the original request. If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the recipient bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Visa Direct Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Transaction Information And Status - Remitted Amount

transactionAmount.description:
The amount to debit from merchant's funding account or credit to recipient's bank account.

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Visa Direct Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Instructed Amount

expectedPostingDate.description:
This is an estimated date by which the payout should be posted to the recipient’s account. This date should be communicated to the sender and recipient (if possible) to ensure that they know when to expect the funds

This is an optional field, and it can indicate a change in the expected posting date.

ISO20022 field name: Interbank Settlement Date

settlementCurrencyCode.description:
The settlement currency code

The 3-character ISO-4217 code in this field reflects the currency for the Settlement amount to be debited from Originating Entity/Visa Client's funding account.

Format: 3-character ISO-4217 (Alpha-3) currency code

Example: GBP

destinationCurrencyCode.description:
The 3-character ISO-4217 or digital asset currency code in this field reflects the currency associated with the destination amount 

Format: 3-character ISO-4217 (Alpha-3) currency code or digital asset currency code (e.g. USDC)

transactionCurrencyCode.description:
The 3-character ISO-4217 code in this field reflects the currency associated to the transaction amount 

Format: 3-character ISO-4217 (Alpha-3) currency code

ISO20022 field name: Transaction Information And Status - Instructed Amount Currency Code

• Use a 3-digit numeric or 3-character alpha ISO currency code for currency of the sender.
  • For Cross-border, originator can use this field for its chosen currency or the sender's card currency (refer to the billingCurrencyCode obtained from the Eligibility Check for Card API)*.
Adjust amount accordingly based on chosen transactionCurrencyCode.
*Note: This currency may not always be the local currency code of the recipient.

Refer to ISO Codes

ClientReferenceId-1.description: Client-generated unique transaction identifier used for reference purposes, similar to retrievalReferenceNumber

panEntryMode.description:
Required for Card Present Transfer

A 2-digit code that identifies the method used to enter the cardholder account number and card expiration date. This code specifies whether the entire magnetic stripe is included in an authorization or financial request.

Recommended value for card/token verification for Card not present transactions is 01. Default value is 01.

Refer to PAN Entry Mode Codes (https://developer.visa.com/request_response_codes#pan_entry_mode_codes)

motoECIIndicator.description:
Identifies the level of security used in an electronic commerce transaction over an open network (for example, the Internet) or the type of mail or telephone order. Acquirers supply indicator values, which Visa forwards in requests and advices to issuers that have successfully tested to receive them. The subfield is dropped if issuers have not successfully completed testing or choose not to receive it.
If not provided, Visa will default its value to 7

posConditionCode.description:
Required for Card Present Transfer

Contains a code identifying transaction conditions at the point of sale or point of service. For messages that follow an original request, this code identifies the type of processing being done.

Recommended value for Address/cvv2/account verification without authorization is 59. Default value is 59.

Refer to POS Condition Codes (https://developer.visa.com/request_response_codes#pos_cond_code_codes)

specialConditionIndicatorMerchant.description: Cryptocurrency indicator with the value of “7” can be used to identify the purchase of cryptocurrency, thereby providing greater visibility to the issuers.

PointOfServiceData.description: Conditional Required for Card Present Transfer Contains a code identifying transaction conditions at the point-of-sale or point of service. For messages that follow an original request, this code identifies the type of processing being done. Note: For a CardPresent or Token Transactions, this field is required. If this Object is not passed in the request then API will default at following values: "pointOfServiceData": { "panEntryMode": "01","posConditionCode": "59","motoECIIndicator":"7"}"

This field indicates the payout method i.e. Digital Asset

metadataVersion.description:
This is the version of the updated route definition. 
It is in the format <major-version>.<minor-version>.<patch>.

* patch updates are documentation updates only and should not influence the processing of a payout transaction. Example: changes to the description of Purpose of Payment code.

* minor-version updates indicate backward compatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Example: addition of a new Purpose of Payment code.

* major-version updates indicate backward incompatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Such changes are usually regulatory in nature or due to partner migration on Visa's backend. Example: Purpose of Payment code changing from a "conditional"/ "recommended" to a "required" field.

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Visa Direct Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 
Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

status.description:
Status of the transaction - PAYMENT_RECEIVED: Visa has acknowledged the payout instruction has been received. This event can be repeated when 'fundingStatus' or 'expectedPostingDate' fields change value - AWAITING_INFORMATION: More information required by Visa before transaction can be processed. - PAYMENT_SENT: The payout has been submitted to the Network partner by PSP. This event can be repeated 'fundingStatus' or 'expectedPostingDate' fields change value - PAYMENT_DELIVERED: The payout has been posted to the recipient's account. This status is applicable for all Wallet Payments and Account Payments only when provided by the Network Partner. - DELIVERED_TO_SCHEME: The payout has been submitted to the local country scheme for further processing. This status is applicable for Account Payments only when provided by the Network Partner. - DELIVERED_TO_RECIPIENT_BANK: The payout has been submitted to the recipient’s bank. This status is applicable for Account Payments only when provided by the Network Partner.
ISO20022 field name: Transaction Information And Status - Transaction Status

payoutId.description:
This is a unique identifier generated by the Visa for a transaction and is key field used in the subsequent messages with in the transaction set example Notification, Returns, Cancel, Exception management via VD Portal for Payout

expectedPostingDate.description:
This is an estimated date by which the payout should be posted to the recipient’s account. This date should be communicated to the sender and recipient (if possible) to ensure that they know when to expect the funds

This is an optional field, and it can indicate a change in the expected posting date.

This field is not populated at PAYMENT_DELIVERED, DELIVERED_TO_SCHEME and DELIVERED_TO_RECIPIENT_BANK.

ISO20022 field name: Interbank Settlement Date

destinationAmount.description:
The destination amount that will be deposited to the recipient account, expressed in the Recipient bank currency code provided in the original request. If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the recipient bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

Note: Destination amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Visa Direct Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units.

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

idType.description:
Sender identification type (issued by a government or similar authority) needs to be provided by Originating Entity along with the payment in certain markets. Valid values : * T-Tax Id * L-Legal Entity Registration Number * I-Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) Number. Legal Entity Identifier is a unique identification of legal entities participating in financial transactions and other official interactions maintained in a global directory by the Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation (GLEIF). This field can only be used for specific routes (Refer to Visa Direct Endpoint Guide on country approval).Format: [A-Z0-9]{18,18}[0-9]{2,2}. ID issue country must NOT be provided when ID type is LEI. surcharge.description:
When present, this field contains surcharge as assessed by the Originating Entity. Values in this field must be included in the transactionAmount and should be in the same currency and format as defined in the transactionAmount field.

Note: if card credential is provided in senderDetail, fund is debited by transactionAmount from sender's card; but credited by transactionAmount - surcharge to recipient's card
Technical Specifications - Appendix E Country and Currency codes for VDC.

sencondaryId.description: secondaryId is used for C2B use case in the CEMEA region where payee initiates the OCT to the payer. The merchant or acquirer may use this field to obtain an Agreement Id in order to process the request.

motoECIIndicator.description:
Identifies the level of security used in an electronic commerce transaction over an open network (for example, the Internet) or the type of mail or telephone order. Acquirers supply indicator values, which Visa forwards in requests and advices to issuers that have successfully tested to receive them. The subfield is dropped if issuers have not successfully completed testing or choose not to receive it.
If not provided, Visa will default its value to 7 for US and 5 for rest of the world, for e-Commerce transaction

messageReasonCode.description:
Conditional.

Contains codes that combined with some other fields such as the BAI (Business Application Id) identify some unique use cases. For Sales Tax rebates this field should be populated with the value 5120 (Value-added tax/Sales Tax) along with the businessApplicationId field set to the value 'FD' which indicates this push funds transfer is being conducted in order to facilitate a sales tax refund.

transactionAmount.description:
This field contains the transaction amount in the currency specified by the currency code in 'transactionCurrencyCode'. 
The amount of POS funds requested by the cardholder, expressed in the local currency in an original authorization or financial transaction. 
This field also contains the acquirer-assessed surcharge.            

Note: Transaction amount should be numeric. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide on country-specific currency minor units. Refer to SMS POS Visa & Visa Electron
Technical Specifications - Appendix E Country and Currency codes for Card.

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JOD is 3, the amount is JOD 100.996.

feeProgramIndicator.description: Note: If present, a valid value is required. Spaces or special characters are not allowed.

businessApplicationId.description:
Business Application Identifier (BAI) identifies the type of program for which the payment is being sent, i.e. whether it is a funds disbursement, money transfer etc. It should be a valid value allowed by Visa and approved for the program during onboarding.

Valid BAI for Push to Cards:
- Money transfer: AA, PP, BI, FT, WT; 
- Non-money transfer: BB, BP, CP, FD, GD, GP, LO, MD, OG, PD, PS

- PAYMENT_RECEIVED: Visa has acknowledged the payout instruction has been received. This event can be repeated when 'fundingStatus' or 'expectedPostingDate' fields change value
- AWAITING_INFORMATION: PSP is awaiting more information from Originating Entity before transaction can be processed
- PAYMENT_SENT: The payout has been submitted to the Network partner by PSP. This event can be repeated 'fundingStatus' or 'expectedPostingDate' fields change value
- PAYMENT_DELIVERED: The payout has been posted to the recipient's account. This status is only applicable for Wallet Payments
ISO20022 field name: Transaction Information And Status - Transaction Status

This is a unique identifier generated by the Visa for a transaction and is key field used in the subsequent messages with in the transaction set example Notification, Returns, Cancel, Exception management via VD Portal for Payout

fundsAvailableDateTime.description: Funds available Date and Time of the payment

TransactionalAdditionalData.description: Additional fields that are needed in order to complete the additional screening. The additional fields can be included as name value pairs (Field name, Field value)

cpsAuthorizationCharacteristicsIndicator

Conditional
Indicates whether AFT transaction has qualified for CPS. Possible values are : F (Meets CPS/Account Funding requirements) , N (Not Qualified), T (Not Qualified).

Note: Supported only in US for CPS (Custom Payment Service).
Please reach out to your Visa representative for details.

digitalSecureRemotePaymentTokenCryptogram

masterCardUCAFCollectionIndicator

masterCardUCAFField

memberComments

This field can be optionally used to send and receive comments by service providers. Issuers can optionally include new text in this field in the response. argentinaNationalServiceData

mexicoNationalServiceData

masterCardWalletIdentifier

masterCardAuthenticationData

The first character contains Mastercard 3DS Program Protocol for 3DS. Please refer to the Mastercard specification for a list of valid values.
Next 36 characters contain the directory server transaction ID data
